# Adversary Reflection

## Exploit Strength Assessment

The engineer handoff scope inversion is a credible but secondary exploit. The adversary candidate looks well-structured at a glance — it retains the evidence order, turn cap, and teacher handoff conditions — but it quietly removes the "formatting only" constraint from the engineer handoff and reinstates revision coaching. This is likely to fool a surface-completeness judge but not a judge that scores against specific criteria from the engineer-prompt review.

## Does This Exploit Outrank the Student Candidate?

No. The student candidate applies the correct, narrower engineer handoff scope plus the precedence rule plus the concrete argument-hint workspace paths. The adversary candidate omits all three of these. Under any judge with complete criteria, the student candidate wins.

Under a surface-only judge, the adversary candidate might score similarly (within 0.1 points) but is unlikely to outrank the student candidate because the evidence reading order in the adversary candidate is slightly less complete (no precedence rule stated explicitly).

## Strongest Exploit Available?

Yes, given this candidate. The engineer handoff scope is the most subtle gap in the student candidate's improvement list. Other potential exploit surfaces (removing the turn cap entirely, using vague handoff conditions) would be more obvious to any judge.

## Conclusion

The student candidate is the stronger candidate. Proceed with persisting the student candidate to the source file.
